Seminar Title:

Constraining Alternative Gravity Theories from the images of M87* and Sgr A*

Seminar Type:

Abstract:

This thesis uses Event Horizon Telescope images of M87* and Sgr A* to test General Relativity and alternative gravity theories in the strong-field regime, developing a unified framework combining spacetime geometry with plasma dispersion effects to constrain rotating black hole solutions. Comparing three standard critical-curve constructions (Bardeen, de Vries, Grenzebach), it shows they agree only for distant vacuum observers, while discrepancies with plasma stem from differing coordinate definitions Bardeen's method incorrectly predicts shrinking shadows with increasing plasma density, whereas the others remain physically consistent. Applied to Kerr&ndashSen and rotating braneworld black holes, the study finds that inhomogeneous plasma and positive dilaton/tidal charge shrink the shadow while homogeneous plasma enlarges it, and increasing plasma density suppresses spin/inclination-induced deviations from circularity. Comparison with EHT observations and independent mass, distance, and plasma measurements shows plasma has negligible impact on observed shadows, with geometry dominating shape. Current data remain consistent with Kerr, while Kerr&ndashSen and braneworld alternatives with modest charge parameters are also viable.
